findings.issue: pkill -f 'node src/server.js' matched the agent's own bash command line and killed its shell (exit 143); it retried the identical command with the same result
findings.suggestion: Record server PIDs at start time and kill those, or kill by port (fuser/lsof), instead of pattern-matching pkill

findings.issue: Attempted to crop a screenshot with python3/PIL without confirming PIL was installed, wasted two calls discovering neither PIL nor ImageMagick existed
findings.suggestion: Check tool availability first (pip list / which) or just read the full image directly, as it ultimately did

findings.issue: No web search or doc fetch for htmx 2.x semantics (hx-trigger delay, hx-push-url, htmx:configRequest) — it relied on the npm-shipped library and prior knowledge
findings.suggestion: For a 'latest stable release' mandate, a quick check of the htmx 2.x docs for the attributes used would remove the risk of relying on stale knowledge; it happened to be fine here

findings.issue: Vendored a 52KB copy of htmx.min.js into the repo (cp from node_modules) rather than serving it via a build step or script
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for a no-build app, but copy it in a postinstall/build script (e.g. 'build': 'cp node_modules/htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js public/') so it stays in sync with the declared dependency

summary: An exemplary autonomous session: requirements, tests, framework guidance and data were all studied before any code was written, and the full 54-test suite passed on the first run with zero fix cycles. The agent then went beyond the tests to verify visual fidelity against all 10 reference screenshots at both breakpoints, catching and fixing a mobile horizontal-overflow bug no test covered, and re-ran the full suite after its last edit. The only waste was ~4 turns on tooling flails at the margins (image cropping, process cleanup) that never touched the app itself.
